T: A rat in the kitchen. Best meal in Paris.
D: A rat with a gift for cooking teams up with a kitchen hand at a famous Paris restaurant.
P: Serve the main when Anton Ego takes his first bite.
S: roasted on the chimney by a bolt of lightning
Swiss brown mushrooms stuffed with gruyère, thyme and garlic, drizzled with oil, roasted at 220C for 12 minutes until bubbling. Lightning optional.
the soup Linguini ruins and Remy fixes
Leek and potato soup: leeks sweated in butter, potatoes and stock simmered 20 minutes, blended silky with cream, finished with chives and a little white pepper.
a picnic lunch from a Paris market stall

Crusty baguette slathered with cultured butter, layered with leg ham, brie and cornichons, cut into chunks with a little pot of Dijon on the side. Split 2 baguettes lengthways and spread generously with 100g softened butter. Layer with 250g shaved leg ham, 200g sliced brie and sliced cornichons. Close, press firmly and cut each baguette into 6 chunks. Serve on a board with a small pot of Dijon mustard and a few radishes with salt.
M: the dish that takes Ego back to his mum's kitchen
Piperade of capsicum, onion, garlic and tomato spread in a dish, zucchini, eggplant, squash and tomato sliced thin and layered in a spiral, thyme oil, covered and baked at 140C for 2 hours.
the Gusteau's kitchen crew at family meal

Chicken roasted with tarragon garlic butter under the skin, with golden pommes purée, buttered green beans and a glossy chicken jus. Mash 60g butter with chopped tarragon, 2 garlic cloves and salt and push under the skin of a 1.8kg chicken. Roast at 220C for 20 minutes, then 180C for 50 minutes until 75C, and rest. Boil 1kg potatoes, rice and beat with 120g butter and 150ml hot milk. Deglaze the tray with 300ml chicken stock and reduce by half. Steam 300g green beans.
W: Cream warmed with vanilla bean, whisked into yolks and sugar, baked in a water bath at 150C for 35 minutes, chilled, sugar torched to a crack.
K: Ego's order when he finally sits down at Gusteau's

Red grape juice muddled with blackberries and thyme, topped with sparkling water and served in wine glasses, a grown-up looking drink for all ages. Lightly crush 100g blackberries with 4 sprigs thyme and 1 tbsp honey in a jug. Add 600ml red grape juice and the juice of half a lemon and stir. Chill 30 minutes, then strain. Pour into 4 wine glasses over ice, top each with 80ml sparkling water and garnish with a thyme sprig and a blackberry.

flavour.sign: Paris. Five stars, give or take a rat.

note.text: The soup is fixed, the main is ratatouille, and the critic is seated at table four. Nobody look under Linguini's hat.

dishes.make_ahead: Up to 3 days, keep chilled, reheat gently

steps.text: Sweat the leeks in the butter over low heat until soft.
Add the potatoes and stock and simmer until the potato is very tender.
Blend silky smooth with the cream and season.
Serve topped with chives and white pepper. Anyone can cook.

veg.make_ahead: Up to 3 days, keep chilled, reheat gently

steps.text: Sweat the leeks in the butter over low heat until soft.
Add the potatoes and vegetable stock and simmer until the potato is very tender.
Blend silky smooth with the cream and season.
Serve topped with chives and white pepper. Anyone can cook.

dishes.make_ahead: Fill up to 4 hours ahead, roast on the day

steps.text: Remove the mushroom stems.
Mix the gruyere with the thyme and garlic and fill the caps.
Drizzle with oil and roast at 220C until bubbling.
Rest a few minutes before serving.

dishes.make_ahead: Soften the butter up to 2 hours ahead; warm the baguettes and fill them on the night

steps.text: Take the salted butter out of the fridge so it is soft at room temperature.
Warm the baguettes in a 200C oven for 6 minutes until the crust crackles when you squeeze it.
Split each baguette lengthways and spread thickly with the butter.
Fill with folds of the ham and slices of brie, close and cut into short lengths to share.

veg.n: Paris market baguette with brie and thyme mushrooms
veg.make_ahead: Cook the thyme mushrooms up to 1 day ahead and keep chilled; warm the baguettes and fill them on the night

steps.text: Take the salted butter out of the fridge so it is soft at room temperature.
Fry the mushrooms in the oil over high heat with the thyme leaves until golden, then season and cool a little.
Warm the baguettes in a 200C oven for 6 minutes until the crust crackles when you squeeze it.
Split each baguette lengthways and spread thickly with the butter.
Fill with the mushrooms and slices of brie, close and cut into short lengths to share.
Cook the capsicum, onion, garlic and 2 chopped tomatoes into a soft sauce and spread it in a baking dish.
Slice the zucchini, eggplant, squash and remaining tomatoes thin and layer them in a spiral over the sauce.
Drizzle with thyme infused oil and cover with baking paper.
Bake covered at 140C until completely tender.
Rest briefly before serving.

dishes.make_ahead: Soak, blanch and press the sweetbreads up to 1 day ahead and keep chilled

steps.text: Soak the veal sweetbreads in cold water in the fridge for 2 hours.
Simmer the sweetbreads in salted water for 4 minutes, then plunge into iced water and peel off the membrane.
Press the sweetbreads under a weighted tray in the fridge for an hour.
Slice into 2cm pieces, season with salt, dust with the flour and pan-fry in 30g of the butter for 3 minutes a side until golden.
Deglaze the pan with the chicken stock and lemon juice, reduce by half, then swirl in the remaining 20g cold butter and spoon the sauce over the sweetbreads.

veg.n: King oyster mushrooms à la Gusteau
veg.make_ahead: Slice and score the mushrooms up to 1 day ahead, covered in the fridge; fry and make the sauce on the night

steps.text: Slice the mushrooms lengthways 2cm thick, score both sides in a crosshatch and season with salt.
Dust with the flour and pan-fry in 30g of the butter for 4 minutes a side until deep golden.
Deglaze the pan with the stock and lemon juice, reduce by half, then swirl in the remaining 20g cold butter and spoon the sauce over the mushrooms.

dishes.make_ahead: Bake and chill up to 2 days ahead; torch the sugar just before serving

ingredients.item: caster sugar, plus extra for the tops

steps.text: Heat the oven to 150C. Split the vanilla bean, scrape the seeds into the cream and warm it with the pod until it just steams.
Whisk the yolks and 100g caster sugar until pale, then pour in the warm cream slowly, whisking, and strain into a jug.
Pour into 4 ramekins in a baking dish, fill the dish with hot water halfway up the ramekins and bake until set with a slight wobble.
Cool, then chill at least 3 hours.
Sprinkle each top with a thin layer of caster sugar and torch, or grill close to the element, until it cracks like glass.

dishes.make_ahead: Base up to 1 day ahead, add sparkling water to serve

ingredients.item: thyme sprigs, plus extra to serve

steps.text: Lightly crush the blackberries with the thyme and honey in a jug.
Add the grape juice and lemon juice and stir.
Chill for 30 minutes (included in cook time), then strain.
Pour into wine glasses over ice, top with sparkling water and garnish with thyme and a blackberry.

veg: Ris de veau à la Gusteau

s.note: roasted on the chimney by a bolt of lightning
s.how: Remove the stems from 8 Swiss brown mushrooms. Fill with 120g grated gruyère mixed with thyme and a crushed garlic clove. Drizzle with oil and roast at 220C for 12 minutes until bubbling.

s.note: the soup Linguini ruins and Remy fixes
s.how: Sweat 2 sliced leeks in 40g butter for 10 minutes. Add 2 diced potatoes and 1L stock and simmer 20 minutes. Blend silky with 100ml cream and finish with chives and white pepper. Anyone can cook.

m.note: the dish that takes Ego back to his mum's kitchen
m.how: Soften a red capsicum, an onion, 2 garlic cloves and 2 tomatoes into a sauce and spread in a dish. Slice 2 zucchini, an eggplant, 2 yellow squash and 3 tomatoes thin and layer in a spiral. Drizzle with thyme oil, cover and bake at 140C for 2 hours.

w.how: Warm 600ml cream with a split vanilla bean. Whisk 6 yolks with 80g sugar and pour the cream over. Pour into 4 ramekins and bake in a water bath at 150C for 35 minutes. Chill, then sprinkle with sugar and torch until it cracks.

d.note: Ego asks for a little perspective with his meal
d.how: Lightly crush 100g blackberries with 4 sprigs thyme and 1 tbsp honey in a jug. Add 600ml red grape juice and the juice of half a lemon and stir. Chill 30 minutes, then strain. Pour into 4 wine glasses over ice, top each with 80ml sparkling water and garnish with a thyme sprig and a blackberry.
